sourceDesc.p: Comments and notes to 秦律十八種.

p.seg: 粟 does not refer to millet here but to all kinds of grain in general with regard to its expected yield.
輒 means "immediately" in administrative texts like this.
頃數 forms the core of the nominal phrase that is the object of the verb 言.
早 is a misspelling of 旱.
Both 𧈸 (zhong) and 䖵 (kun) are umbrella terms for flying and crawling creatures that harm the crop.
Following 戰國秦漢簡帛古書通假字彙纂, 450a-b, and 非簡帛類戰國文字通假材料的整理與研究, 175, we read 夜 as a loan for zhì 炙, "to burn".
Following Shuihudi Qin mu zhujian, 2001, transcription, p. 20, n. 4, we understand 生荔 as referring to unripe and shell-covered shoots of plants.
Following Shuihudi Qin mu zhujian, 2001, transcription, p. 20, we understand 綰享 as a loan for 棺槨.
Following Shuihudi Qin mu zhujian, 2001, transcription, p. 21, n. 10, we understand 河 as a loan for 呵.
Since this is a regulation addressed at officials, the lexical aspect of many verbs is tolerative.

The two normalized characters 穌 and 藶 should be inserted into the fourth and sixth position: 芻自黃穌及藶束以上皆受之。See Shuihuidi Qin mu zhujian 2001, transcriptions, p. 21, n. 3. For the corresponding inscriptional characters and their transcriptions see https://zi.tools/zi/𳑊 and https://zi.tools/zi/藶.
Read 勿 as a loan for wú 無, "not have".
This addresses the husbander of the fields and his assistants and not the people who are selling alcohol!
Following Shuihudi Qin mu zhujian (2001: 22), we read 旱 as a loan for 皂.

Here, the line arrangement follows the mistaken line arrangement of the transcription in Shuihuidi Qin mu zhujian, p. 22. In fact, the document (p. 16) shows a spatium before 殿, which indicates that there should be a line break before this character in the transcription. Basing itself on a note by Gao Heng, the Hanyu da cidian defines 田典 as an official title, referring to a local administrator of fields. However, the context implies that in fact only a person responsible for the use of an ox in one field can be meant, i.e., someone who is responsible for the cultivation of one field. Otherwise, one and the same official would have been rewarded and fined at the same time.

入之其 or 其入之 is considered redundant by Shuihuidi Qin mu zhujian (p. 24) and Hulsewé (1975, p. 28). We beg to disagree, since the initial 其 and the final 者 serve to mark the sentence as a conditional clause, as in the following passage (see Shuoyuan 1): 其榛藂刺虎豹者，吾是以知其勇也. ("If someone charges through thickets to stab tigers and leopards, then I know from that that he is brave.") The second 其 is the pronoun for the subject of the conditional clause.
